summary: Caramelized-raisin sundae: raisins browned in butter with brown sugar and salt for 5 minutes, simmered about 10 minutes with port, orange zest and juice into a sauce that coats a spoon, cooled until warm and spooned over vanilla ice cream with cinnamon-spiced fresh apple; 25 minutes, serves 4.
glance: 1 cup raisins, 1 cup tawny port, brown sugar, butter, orange zest and juice, simmered about 10 minutes
8 scoops of high-quality vanilla ice cream with diced apple and cinnamon
faq: Why do the raisins get so plump?

They grow hilariously plump while cooking, blowing up like little zeppelins, but return to a normal size when they cool. Don't let it worry you; just don't let them burn, though they should brown a bit.
How do I know the sauce is done?
When it is thick enough to coat a spoon, or when dragging a spatula across the bottom of the pan leaves a clear space for a couple of seconds. Cool until slightly warm (about 100°F).
Can I change the sauce?
Puree it for a smooth variation, or use dried figs instead of raisins.
What port should I use?

Tawny port is a good choice, not cooking wine. Avoid fortified wines labeled as cooking wines: they are mass-produced with awful flavors masked by vast amounts of salt. Buy mid-grade bottles for cooking and save expensive aged ones for sipping.
What are the main fortified wines?

Port (Douro valley, Portugal, often red and sweet), Madeira (heated and oxidized), sherry (Jerez, Spain, aged in a solera), Marsala (Sicily, similar to sherry) and vermouth (Italy, herb-scented, white dry or red sweet; dry vermouth keeps a long time in the refrigerator, handy for cooking).

summary: Caramelized pear and ginger scones: diced pears cooked about 8 minutes in butter with ginger and cinnamon, folded into a cold-butter, buttermilk scone dough, shaped into a 24 x 4 1/2-inch rectangle and cut into 12 triangles, and baked about 22 minutes at 400°F; makes 12 in 55 minutes.
glance: 400°F for about 22 minutes, until quite golden brown
1 cup very cold butter cut in until oatmeal-sized pieces for flaky scones
faq: What are these scones like?

Light and moist, with just enough pear and ginger flavor to be interesting but not overpowering. The author's kids beg for them when there's company for brunch, and he says they'd be ridiculously good as the base for strawberry shortcake.
How do I make flaky versus tender scones?
Cut the cold butter into the flour to oatmeal-sized pieces for flaky scones, or blend until fully powdered in a food processor for tender, less flaky scones.
How do I caramelize the pears?

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the diced crisp pears, salt and sugar and cook, stirring, until most of the liquid has cooked off and they begin to brown, about 6 minutes, then add ginger and cinnamon for 2 more. Cool them before adding to the dough.
How much buttermilk?
1 1/2 cups, plus maybe another tablespoon or two, but don't hurry: you want the dough to just barely form a mass. Knead as briefly as possible.
How do I shape them?

Flatten the dough into a rectangle about 24 x 4 1/2 inches, brush with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar, cut into 6 rectangles and divide each into two triangles, leaving two inches between scones on the baking sheets.

summary: Triple-smoky mac and cheese: elbow macaroni cooked to just al dente, a bechamel with smoked paprika, chipotle in adobo and rosemary melted with smoked cheddar and mozzarella, topped with garlic breadcrumbs and baked at 350°F for about 30 minutes; serves 6-8 as a main in 1 hour.
glance: oak-smoked cheddar, smoked paprika and chipotle in adobo
350°F for about 30 minutes in a 9x13 dish
refrigerate, top with breadcrumbs at the last minute, allow extra baking time
faq: What inspired this mac and cheese?

An incredible oak-smoked cheddar the author found at Seattle's Pike Place Market, reinforced with smoked paprika and chipotle in adobo. If you can't get smoked cheddar, use regular cheddar and substitute smoked mozzarella.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, refrigerate it, which is convenient for dinner parties; wait to top with breadcrumbs until the last minute and allow additional baking time to come up to temperature.
How do I cook the macaroni?
Boil it just until it becomes al dente, since it will bake more in the oven, then drain and toss with 2 tablespoons of butter.
How intense should the sauce be?

Pretty intense, since it will be diluted by a full pound of pasta. Taste and adjust: it will probably need a little salt but maybe not too much depending on the cheeses, and add more spiciness if desired.
What mozzarella should I use?
Regular mozzarella, not fresh, grated, with 8 ounces of the smoked cheddar.

summary: Red-wine braised cabbage: onion and leek softened 3 minutes, then red cabbage simmered covered with 1 1/2 cups of dry red wine, caraway and salt for about 20 minutes and uncovered until quite tender and the liquid is reduced to 1/8 inch; vegan, serves 4 in 40 minutes (10 active).
glance: covered about 20 minutes, then uncovered until the liquid is reduced to about 1/8 inch
Vegan and gluten-free (butter optional if you don't need vegan)
faq: What is the key to braised cabbage?

Cook it enough to be meltingly tender, but not so much that it starts to break down. The author's German downstairs neighbor in Milwaukee cooked cabbage for hours until the sulfurous smell penetrated the building, but he still loves well-prepared braised cabbage.
Can I use other cabbage or wine?
Use green cabbage instead of red and replace the red wine with a dry white wine or a dark ale, adding a tablespoon of prepared Dijon mustard in either case.
Do the vegetable sizes matter?
The exact sizes of onion, leek and cabbage aren't critical: use what you have and it will braise down into a luscious pile of tender vegetables.
How do I finish the braise?
After about 20 minutes covered, remove the lid and continue cooking until the cabbage is quite tender and the liquid is reduced to about 1/8 inch on the bottom of the pot.
What do I serve with it?
Crispy polenta cakes with white beans and morels, which the author says is a real treat together.

summary: Cheese-battered onion rings and a stout chocolate malt: extra-sharp cheddar broiled to a frico, ground to a powder and added to a thin tempura-style batter, onion rings fried at 360°F, served with a shake of chocolate ice cream, stout and malted milk powder; the author's playful experiment.
glance: 360°F, in small batches, until golden brown
about 2 cups cheddar broiled, then ground (50 g used; the author would try 75 g)
2 1/2 cups milk chocolate ice cream, 4 ounces stout, 5 tablespoons malted milk powder; four 6-ounce servings
faq: How do you get cheese in an onion ring batter?

The author wanted cheese flavor without a melty mess that would ruin the crunch, so he broiled grated extra-sharp cheddar like a frico on a silpat until it started to brown, cooled it, patted off the oil and ground it to a powder in a spice grinder to add to a tempura-style batter.
What batter is used?

Based on Morimoto's small-batch tempura: egg yolk, oil, salt, flour and seltzer, with an optional big pinch of xanthan gum that really helps cling. It should be rather thin, like crepe batter, not thick pancake batter.
How do I fry the onion rings?

Heat oil to 360°F, dredge each thick ring in flour, shake off the excess, dip in the batter, drip off the excess and fry in small batches until golden brown; chopsticks make it easiest. Drain on paper towels and season with sea salt.
What is the stout chocolate malt?

A shake blended from milk chocolate ice cream, stout or porter (the author used an oatmeal stout) and Carnation malted milk powder. The malt in the beer and the malt powder complement each other; it can be held in the freezer for a while.
Is it an appetizer or a dessert?
The author asks readers: if you served a tiny portion in a multi-course meal, would it be an appetizer or a dessert?

summary: Bunuelos (bimuelos), rustic Sephardic yeast-raised doughnuts: a wet dough risen at least an hour, shaped with wet hands into rough holed rounds and deep fried at 370°F, served with honey at Hanukkah or powdered sugar; makes about 14 in 20 minutes active.
glance: 20 minutes active plus a 1 hour rise
3 inches of oil at 370°F, golden on each side
honey, or powdered sugar for vegan
Vegetarian; vegan option with powdered sugar
faq: What are bunuelos?

A rustic yeast-raised and fried donut that the Sephardic side of the author's family makes: honey at Hanukkah, powdered sugar any other time. There's also a Passover version made with matzoh, which the author says doesn't hold a candle to the flour-based one.
How do I shape the dough?

It should be quite wet and isn't rolled out: moisten your hands, grab about 3 tablespoons of dough, form a rough ball and poke a hole through the center with your thumb, then drop it carefully into the oil. They're meant to be rustic; don't spend time making them perfect.
How do I know my yeast is good?
Stir the yeast into 1 cup of warm water and let it proof; if you don't see bubbles after a few minutes, buy new yeast.
How long can the dough rise?
At least 1 hour in a warm spot; the author has let it go four hours, stirring down occasionally, and it only gets more delicious.
How do I fry them?
Heat 3 inches of oil to 370°F (use a thermometer), fry as many as fit without crowding until golden brown on one side, flip, then drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

summary: Thai-style salad of grilled eggplant, tofu and watermelon with an oil-free lime dressing: soy-marinated tofu and eggplant grilled and tossed with orange-muscat vinegar, over lettuce with red onion, cabbage, chilies, cubed watermelon, mint, Thai basil and cilantro; serves 8 as a side or about 3 as a light meal.
glance: 8 as a side dish or about 3 as a light meal
6 tablespoons lime juice, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sugar; no oil
eggplant planks and tofu planks on a moderate grill with no leaping flames
yield: 8 as a side dish or about 3 as a light meal
faq: Is this Thai, Vietnamese or Cambodian?

The author calls it Thai-style but it could just as easily be Vietnamese or Cambodian. It's ultra-refreshing and, because the dressing is oil-free, very low calorie. It can be part of a larger Southeast Asian spread or a light meal on its own.
Why watermelon in a savory salad?
Watermelon is being used in interesting savory dishes (compressed, juiced, pickled, "sashimi", grilled). Here it gives a beautiful sweet counterpoint to the puckery lime dressing and fresh herbs.
How do I make the salad my own?
Think of it as a basis for improvisation: change the lettuce, use tempeh instead of tofu, add rice noodles, use different herbs, add roasted peanuts.
Do I have to grill?
The author grilled the tofu and eggplant for a bit of smoky flavor, but you can use a frying pan or the oven just as well.
What replaces the muscat vinegar?
If you don't have Trader Joe's mandarin orange muscat champagne vinegar, use the juice of one orange, 2 teaspoons sugar and 2 tablespoons rice vinegar to toss with the warm eggplant.

summary: Risotto cake with crispy ramps and a fried egg: leftover risotto formed into a 3.5-inch patty and fried golden in butter, topped with a fried egg with a liquid yolk and ramp whites fried until well browned, finished with oregano and aged balsamic; makes 1 serving.
glance: 6, white parts only, halved lengthwise, fried in butter until well browned
1/2 cup leftover risotto formed into a 3.5-inch, 1/2-inch-thick patty
fried until the white is set and the yolk liquid
faq: What are ramps?

A classic spring food, along with asparagus, morels, fiddlehead ferns and eggs: they look like scallions with a big green leaf on top, are in the allium family, and have an intense garlicky aroma and flavor that inspires passionate devotees. Appalachian towns hold ramp festivals with Ramp Queens and eating contests.
How do I make risotto cakes?

Whenever the author makes risotto he makes extra for cakes the next day. Usually it holds together enough to fry without additions, but if it's falling apart stir in a beaten egg. A ring mold helps form it neatly.
What if I have no leftover risotto?
Use grilled toast (brioche, ideally) or a savory French toast.
Can I use the ramp greens?
The author used only the white parts, but the greens would make a pesto that would be a beautiful addition.
How do I fry the egg?

In the same pan with a little more butter, until the white is done and the yolk liquid; adding a little water and covering the pan helps cook the top of the white. Use your own judgment about undercooked eggs.

summary: Manouri cheese blintzes: a thin blender batter cooked on one side only in a 7-inch pan, filled with a sweet lemon manouri (or ricotta) filling, folded like a burrito and fried in butter until golden; makes about 30 small blintzes, serves 6, and can be filled and refrigerated 24 hours ahead.
glance: 2 cups flour, cornstarch, water, milk, 7 eggs; blend 3 minutes, rest at least 30 minutes
about 1 minute, 2-3 tablespoons batter in a 7-inch pan, don't flip
sour cream and brown sugar, or rosemary-blueberry sauce
faq: What is manouri cheese?
A Greek sheep's milk cheese with a sweet, clean, dairy taste and a texture very similar to drained ricotta. If you can't get it, use ricotta and reduce or eliminate the milk in the filling.
Can I make blintzes ahead?
Yes: make the pancakes, fill and roll them, then refrigerate the filled blintzes for up to 24 hours until ready to fry in butter and serve.
Are blintzes hard to make?
They're very forgiving: they don't need to be as thin as crepes, and rolling hides any imperfections. A fair bit of work, but much can be done ahead, ideal for a brunch with friends.
How do I cook and fill the pancakes?

Ladle 2-3 tablespoons of batter into a lightly buttered pan over medium-low heat, tilting to spread, cook about 1 minute until well set and don't flip. Put a heaping tablespoon of filling about 1 inch from the front edge, fold the front over, fold in the sides and roll up like a burrito.
How do I finish them?
Fry in batches in a generous amount of butter over a medium flame until golden brown and crispy on each side, keeping the flame low enough that the filling cooks by the time the wrapper is done.

summary: Hatch chiles stuffed with cilantro scrambled eggs: peppers roasted in a 400°F toaster oven until blackened, peeled without rinsing and seeded, then filled with eggs scrambled slowly over low heat for at least 10 minutes with cilantro and optional jalapeno; makes 4 stuffed peppers.
glance: 4 large Hatch chiles, green or ripe, or poblanos
6 eggs with 1/4 cup milk, cooked over low heat at least 10 minutes
steamed corn tortillas, refried black beans, pico de gallo
faq: What are Hatch chiles?

A specialty of the Mesilla Valley area of New Mexico, where a huge festival celebrates the annual harvest and roasting season. In the Seattle area, Alvarez Farms brings them to farmer's markets in early fall. They're most often used green, but this time they had ripe red ones.
Why are ripe peppers red?
All peppers, from a big bell to a tiny Thai bird chile, are red when ripe; a green pepper was picked before it was fully ripe, which gives it a different flavor profile.
How do I scramble eggs for big custardy curds?

Slow and low: egg cookery is about temperature control, because if they get too hot the proteins knot up and become tough. Work over very low heat, folding and moving the cooked egg off the bottom of the pan, for at least 10 minutes.
How do I roast and peel the chiles?

Roast in a 400°F toaster oven (or regular oven, grill or over a gas flame with tongs) until mostly blackened, steam in a covered bowl until cool, peel without rinsing (you'd lose flavor), and slit one side to remove the ribs and seeds.
Can I use other peppers?
Poblanos or any other big, mild pepper. "Relleno" just means stuffed, and moving the eggs from a batter on the outside to a creamy filling inside is the idea.
